evidence: Reviewed the induction that minimum current head is minimum globally remaining occurrence and that advancing one run preserves ordered permutation.
Reviewed run/pass recurrence, traffic derivation, stability, capacity, predecessor deletion, restart, and atomic publication reasoning.
proof_review.notes: The executable is an in-memory semantic reference, not storage, crash, or performance evidence.

evidence: Audited theorem, model, invariant, expected, adversarial, historical, stable, durable, atomic, verified, logical, and physical language.
Separated abstract I/O, merge mechanism, filesystem/object-store policy, and empirical machine behavior.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No local rename or flush behavior is claimed universally across storage systems.

evidence: The CPython 3.14.4 snippet produced exact run counts, sorted output, stage count, and 102 logical item transfers on macOS 13.7.8 x86_64.
Independent bounded merge configurations and exercise calculations passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution does not establish I/O, buffer capacity, filesystem semantics, compression, durability, fault tolerance, or production performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed ordering contract, run generation, replacement selection, multiway merge, fan-in, pass planning, temporary space, parallelism, distribution sorting, variable records, recovery, validation, and evidence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed byte budgets, buffer and descriptor limits, stable ties, comparator versioning, checksums, compression, storage topology, concurrency, short I/O, immutable lineage, crash points, cleanup, telemetry, and publication.

pedagogical_review.notes: The Level-II chapter derives pass geometry and I/O, executes stable multiway merging, connects proof to recovery and storage constraints, supplies ten distinct examples, and ends with five progressive exercises and complete answers.

limitations: Internal source, mathematical, snippet, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical review only; no external academic, database, storage, filesystem, object-store, distributed-systems, performance, regulatory, or operational review is claimed. Conclusions remain conditional on snapshot, comparator, representation, stability, N/M/B, fan-in, storage topology, buffer and temporary capacity, concurrency, compression, checksum, durability, recovery, toolchain, machine, and workload assumptions.
